_what: Realized availability 2023-2025 for every player priced inside pick 150 on the 2026 board, against the board's `games_expected`.
_source: nflverse weekly ROSTERS, status == ACT — the availability record. NOT the weekly stats file: an active player who records nothing has no stats row, and that happens on 39.4% of active QB weeks and 27.4% of TE weeks league-wide, so the stats file answers 'did he record anything' rather than 'was he available'. Measured both ways inside the top 150 and the choice moves each position by <= 0.27 games, because these are starters — but the check had to be run, not assumed.
_route: stats_player / roster_weekly parquets fetched DIRECTLY from the nflverse release. `nfl_data_py.import_weekly_data` 404s for 2025 because the release is named `stats_player`, not `player_stats`; the data was there the whole time.
_caveats: SURVIVORSHIP: the cut conditions on being priced inside pick 150 on the 2026 board, so players whose careers ended are absent. That biases realized games UPWARD, i.e. AGAINST the conclusion below, so the real over-statement is if anything larger.
Mean of per-season means — a one-season player weighs as much as a three-season one.
K n=3. Do not lean on the kicker figure.
11 of 146 draftable players have no NFL history at all (rookies) and are ABSENT rather than zero.

absence_shape._what: WHY the positions differ in availability: frequency vs duration, measured separately because a single games-played number cannot distinguish them and the two imply different draft-day risks.
absence_shape._finding: DURATION IS FLAT. League-wide the mean COMPLETED absence is 3.67 weeks at QB, 3.35 RB, 3.24 TE, 3.12 WR — a 0.55-week spread across four positions on 320-1111 spells each — and 21-24% of spells run to the end of the season at every position. FREQUENCY is where the positions part company.

QB.caveat: mean_completed uses only absences observed to END. 77 of 320 spells are RIGHT-CENSORED — they were still running when the season stopped, so their true length is unknown and at least what is recorded. Pooling them into one mean biases E[weeks out] low, worst for the severe injuries this term prices.

where_the_constant_is_furthest_from_the_._what: Draftable players with >=2 seasons of history, ranked by how far their OWN realized availability sits from the single positional constant the board assigns them.
where_the_constant_is_furthest_from_the_._how_to_read_it: THIS IS HISTORY, NOT A FORECAST, and the difference matters. It does not say these players will miss games in 2026; it says the board currently assumes they will play the positional average and their own record says otherwise. That is an argument for a PER-PLAYER prior, not for fading these names. Two-season players regress hardest — Nabers is 14 then 4, which is one injured season out of two, and a mean of 9.0 carries almost no information about a third.

per_player_prior._what: `expected_games` run for real: a per-player expected-games prior at three shrinkage settings, which is the object that would replace one constant per position.
per_player_prior._the_decision_is_shrink_k: k weights the position prior in SEASON UNITS: k=1 says one observed season is worth as much as the prior. DECLARED, NOT FITTED — I have not tuned it to make any number come out, and it is a parameter because choosing it prices the board, which is not the ingest's job. k=None is the raw history and is NOT a drop-in: it takes Jonathon Brooks (one rookie season, three games, torn ACL) to 3.00 against an RB prior of 14.2.
per_player_prior._even_at_k_1_the_one_season_players_move: Theo Wease -6.50 and Jonathon Brooks -5.60 on a SINGLE season each. That is the case this function's own docstring warns about, and it is unresolved at every k tried — it argues for weighting by seasons observed rather than for a different global k, which is again A's call.

_provenance._what: Which nflverse assets these numbers came from. nflverse REVISES completed seasons occasionally — its own census says so — and without this there is no way to tell which revision a figure was measured on. Byte size and row count are two independent handles on that.

reproduced.result: EXACT. Re-derived `durability` from the weekly-roster assets recorded above and compared against this file: 135 of 135 draftable players, 0 differences in mean games or seasons observed, and the by_position summary recomputed from the player rows agrees with the stored one.
reproduced._caveat: Needs the parquet assets, which are not in the repo, so it runs where they are rather than in CI. `projection_spread_vs_realized` has NOT been reproduced this way — it depends on the scoring mapper as well as the roster, and the fumble gap parked for A sits inside that path.
